title: Dynamic MCP schema and governed surface projections

phases.objective: Define deterministic public surface projection contracts that consume authoritative runtime decisions and readiness evidence without creating a second authority or connection-selection path.

e2e_journeys.actor: Tenant-facing GPT or Remote MCP surface
e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Authoritative context, capability, authority, plan, readback, and readiness contracts
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The surface returns a bounded no-secret projection or fails closed when authoritative contracts, readiness, or tenant binding are missing.
steps: Receive the resolved context and capability manifest from the upstream runtime contract.
Receive preflight, plan, approval or delegation, final authority, execution, adapter, readback, and readiness evidence without deriving replacements locally.
Project only allowlisted identity, capability, blocker, questionnaire, readback, and public-result fields.
Ignore caller-provided identity as an authority source.
Reject a Remote MCP projection when the authoritative result is not bound to the requested workspace.
Reject write-tool projection on the Track C read-only consumer boundary.
assertions: The surface does not mint execution authority.
The surface does not select a connection.
The surface does not execute a provider.
Caller identity cannot widen the authoritative tenant or workspace context.
Sensitive questionnaire fields and secret-like values are excluded from the public projection.
Missing final authority or readiness evidence fails closed.

phases.objective: Bind the public projection consumer to the Track A runtime contract after Tracks B and A land, then validate exact-head repository and protocol parity without changing generated artifacts on this branch.
Validate exact-head repository gates and upstream contract drift after Tracks B and A land.
Run separately authorized non-production live-client acceptance after exact runtime composition is available.
Complete separately authorized production parity, monitoring, rollback, and post-merge audit.
